en-US.name: wave-mesh
en-US.subtitle: Self-hosted mesh VPN
en-US.promotionalText: Your laptops, servers and clusters in one private network, directly from device to device. On a control server you run yourself, or one we run for you.
en-US.description:
wave-mesh connects your iPhone and iPad with your other devices – laptops, servers, NAS boxes and Kubernetes clusters – in one private network, a wave. Connections run directly from device to device, even behind NAT and without port forwarding.

The app is the client for a wave-mesh control server: one you run yourself, or one Moellenbeck Digital runs for you. Enter its address, approve the device in the browser, and the tunnel starts.

• Reach the devices and services in your wave by name
• End-to-end encrypted with WireGuard®. Private keys are created on the device and never leave it
• Direct connections wherever possible, an encrypted relay where not
• Several waves at once, each paused and resumed on its own
• Connects again by itself after a restart or a network change
• "Check connection" says in plain sentences what works and what does not
• Join from the QR code your control server shows

No analytics, no advertising. The app talks only to the control server you enter; no data is sold or passed on.

You need an account on a wave-mesh control server. How to run one, or have us run it: wave-mesh.org

WireGuard is a registered trademark of Jason A. Donenfeld.

review.notes:
wave-mesh is a mesh VPN client for teams and administrators. It connects the device to a "wave": a private network of the user's own devices, coordinated by a wave-mesh control server that the customer runs themselves or that Moellenbeck Digital runs for them. Traffic between the devices is end-to-end encrypted with WireGuard and flows directly between them. The app does not route general internet traffic and is not a public VPN service. It uses NEPacketTunnelProvider; Moellenbeck-Digital UG is enrolled as an organization.

To test:
1. Open the app and tap Continue on the explanation of what the control server learns.
2. Enter the control server wave.moellenbeck-digital.io and tap Log in.
3. iOS asks whether wave-mesh may add a VPN configuration: allow it.
4. A sign-in page opens. Sign in with the demo account (email and password above).
5. The app shows the demo wave as connected, with this device's name and address in it. "Check connection" lists what works.

The demo wave belongs to this review account only. The same account also signs in to the web interface at https://wave.moellenbeck-digital.io, which lists the device once it has joined.

The app collects no analytics and shows no advertising. It sends the control server the user enters only what joining needs: the device's name, its public keys and the network addresses it can be reached at.
